name.basis: the firm's own site and its Form ADV primary business name (LUX CAPITAL MANAGEMENT, LLC, CRD 163026)

icon_url.basis: Lux's logo is TWO inline SVGs, not one: .logo_embed carries the angled 'Lu' monogram (viewBox 0 0 64 64, currentColor) and .logo_embed-x-char carries the red #FF1C24 cross that stands in for the X, sized 47.875% and absolutely positioned at inset 0 0 auto auto (top right) by lux-capital.webflow.shared.css. Taking only the first yields 'Lu'. The two are composed at the site's own geometry into sources/site/lux-mark-full.svg. The site's declared icon assets are both unusable: the 32x32 shortcut icon would be upscaled and the 256x256 apple-touch webclip is pre-blurred (edge ramp 6.09px against a 2px limit). The composed mark normalizes from the vector at ramp 0.77px, contrast 11.0:1, box 70%, radius 80% -- inside every rule with no override flags, and it fills the circle far better than the monogram alone (artwork 178px in the master against 134px). Preview at sources/site/lux-icon-master-preview.png.

provenance.source_url: https://www.luxcapital.com (two inline SVGs composed into sources/site/lux-mark-full.svg)
provenance.plate: synthesized #ffffff behind a bare glyph (source 85% transparent)

icon_url.flag: the URL here is the origin page; the Icon Images bucket URL replaces it at the gated ingest step (COLLECTION.md §9). Measuring this mark required a fix to the ramp metric in scripts/utils/icon-normalize.ts -- see report.md §13.

founding_year.basis: luxcapital.com captures begin 2000-04-07 and the 2001 site describes the firm as operating; the founders are named on the 2005 team page as co-founders

history.basis: the firm's own portfolio pages across five eras (2005 portfolio.php, the 2012-2016 grid, the 2016-2022 WordPress cards, the 2023+ Webflow cards) plus its news archive and this run's base
history.value: Founded in New York in 2000 by Josh Wolfe, Peter Hébert and Robert Paull, Lux Capital began as a nanotechnology research house as much as a venture firm: its 2001 site described funding "start-up capital, or the first outside funds a company raises" in information technology and nanotechnology, and its first portfolio page (2005) listed seven companies, among them Nanosys, Molecular Imprints, Cambrios and the firm's own spin-out Lux Research. That habit of building as well as backing runs through the book — the firm's pages record Genocea as "founded by Lux in 2006 as a spin-out of Harvard Medical School", Kala Pharmaceuticals as a Johns Hopkins spin-out it founded, and Everspin as a spin-out it ideated and helped lead out of Freescale. The modern firm is a deep-tech and defence investor writing first checks: Anduril (2017), Applied Intuition (2017), Zoox (2015), Planet (2013), Relativity Space (2016), Saildrone (2016), Varda (2021) and Impulse Space (2022) on the hardware side; Recursion, Eikon, EvolutionaryScale and a large biology book on the science side; and Hugging Face (Series A, 2019), Runway, Together, Sakana AI, Cognition and Physical Intelligence in AI. Exits include Auris Health (Johnson & Johnson, 2019), CTRL-labs (Facebook, 2019), MosaicML (Databricks, 2023), Nervana (Intel, 2016), Luxtera (Cisco, 2019), Kurion (Veolia, 2016) and a cohort that listed by SPAC in 2020-21 (Desktop Metal, Matterport, Aeva, Rigetti, Evolv, Shapeways, Latch, Science 37). Lux Ventures IX closed at $1.5B in January 2026, the firm's largest fund.

investment_concept.basis: the firm's own industry vocabulary (Engineering + Electronics, Physics + Aerospace, Securing Life + Environment, Advancing Human Health, Infrastructure + Computer Science) reconciled with the landed focus distribution
investment_concept.value: Backs scientists and engineers building companies at the edges of the possible -- defence and aerospace, robotics and advanced manufacturing, semiconductors and photonics, biology and health, and the computing infrastructure underneath them. Lux writes first institutional checks and frequently co-founds or incubates companies out of university and corporate research, then follows into later rounds through dedicated opportunity and co-invest vehicles.

investment_stage.basis: the landed entry_stage distribution over 271 members -- Seed 136, Series A 92, Growth 42, Pre-Seed 1 -- plus the fund architecture (flagship funds alongside Total Opportunities and two Co-Invest Opportunities vehicles that carry the later rounds)
investment_stage.flag: derived from the base and the fund ladder rather than a site filter; Lux publishes no stage filter

investment_geo.basis: hq_country on the landed base: US 249 of 271 (92%), with single rows in Canada, Lithuania, Israel, the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Nigeria, Ghana, Japan and the Bahamas
investment_geo.flag: the geo core is one label; 'other' names the two regions with more than one row

investment_scope.basis: focus from the firm's own site sector tags on 350 base rows, crosswalked to data/taxonomy/focus.json (crosswalk in config.json), published above 12 companies. Scope type is the curated judgement carried in investor.json.

investment_range.basis: median $6.5M is the Form D first-round distribution over the 53 members with issuer coverage (p25 $2.6M, p75 $17.3M, max $108M); the lower limit is the first-check seed floor those filings show (smallest $0.6M); the upper limit is the largest position the fund ladder supports, a 10-15% concentration of the $1.5B Lux Ventures IX
investment_range.flag: a round-size proxy for check size, fair only for a lead investor; Lux leads or co-leads most first rounds but the median is the round, not the check

notable_investments.basis: recognition over the confirmed base only; every name is a ledger-verified member of this run

aum.basis: Form ADV Section 7.B, annual amendment filed 2026-03-31: 17 private funds with $11,237,733,247 of gross assets. Lux Capital Management is an exempt reporting adviser (SEC file 802-75425) and files no Item 5.F regulatory AUM, so both ends of the range are the sworn 7.B composite
aum.flag: press figures sit BELOW the sworn number -- TechCrunch reported '$7 billion' of AUM at the January 2026 close of Lux Ventures IX. Under §11 a press figure below the sworn floor belongs in this flag rather than in the range. The 7.B figure is gross asset value, not committed capital

funds.basis: Form D total offering amounts per vehicle, each asserted against the filing at build time. Lux Ventures IX's $1.5B Form D (filed 2025-12-15) matches the reported January 2026 close to the dollar. Lux Ventures I and II predate electronic Form D and filed on paper (REGDEX), so they carry no size here; the sidecar vehicles (Sidecar, Sidecar II, Entrepreneurs Funds, Special Founders Fund, Cayman III, VIII-B) and the SPAC (Lux Health Tech Acquisition Corp, deregistered without a business combination) are counted in the basis rather than listed

hq_location.basis: issuer address on 21 of 21 of the firm's own Form D filings; unanimous. Filing-grade.

individuals.basis: Live team CMS: 41 members. Positions are CMS titles (33 explicit); untitled members under the investing tabs render as 'Partner', the site's own presentation. 6 names from the 2026 Wayback roster are no longer on the live team page. Socials from profile pages: 15 LinkedIn, 41 X.
